quote: please please tell me Kellina. It's not Michelina. Okay?
stewart_read: Rep mishandles the customer's name repeatedly in the first 30 seconds, a legitimacy/attention-to-detail stumble right after intro.
coaching_implication: Slow down and confirm the name once clearly before proceeding; repeated mispronunciation in the opening seconds undercuts the calm, competent framing the intro needs.

quote: solar is definitely a great way to be able to, switch over to clean energy and, you know, save trees
stewart_read: Rep validates the interest reason but drifts into unsolicited environmental-benefit selling instead of just acknowledging and moving to the next verify item.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as simple rapport-building small talk rather than true scope creep since it's brief and not technical.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the reason and move on faster — the closer sells value, the setter should keep this to a single validating line.

stewart_read: Bill amount captured cleanly, but the rep never uses this number again to build urgency or flip it against the utility.
coaching_implication: Should have reflected the bill back later ('that $2.80 a month is exactly why this makes sense') to anchor the appointment to her pain point.

quote: It's a automatic payment, so I never look at it. You know, it's online.
stewart_read: First touch of the bill-retrieval struggle; rep responds by asking about online kWh access rather than immediately offering a fast alternative.
coaching_implication: Schema calls for pivoting to verbal read-back or deferring to specialist within 2 minutes of friction — first touch is the moment to start that clock.

quote: I would have to get on the site and look. I don't have anything.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same struggle; rep keeps probing for a paper bill instead of pivoting to deferring bill capture to the specialist.
coaching_implication: This is the point to say 'no problem, the specialist can pull that live on the call' rather than continuing to search for a workaround.

quote: just give Pacific Power a call.
stewart_read: Third touch; rep finally offers a concrete alternative (call the utility) but total time spent on this single item is roughly 3 minutes.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic patience could explain persistence if the rep believed the bill was truly required for this lead type, but the time cost outweighs the value of continuing to search live.
coaching_implication: Cap live bill-search attempts and pivot to 'specialist will collect on the call' well before the 3-minute mark.

quote:
what we'll do is we'll set up,
a meeting.
stewart_read: No day or time is ever proposed or agreed to; the call ends without any button-up elements (no hour block, no driving/computer ask, no 'is that fair' handshake).
coaching_implication: Rep needed to immediately follow with a specific day/time offer and lock a verbal handshake before ending the call.

stewart_read: Co-owner (wife) is identified but never invited onto the appointment or even mentioned again.
alternative_hypothesis: Since no appointment time was ever set, there was no explicit moment to exclude the spouse — but the omission still stands given no follow-up mention.
coaching_implication: Once a co-owner is confirmed, the rep should say wife should be included in the specialist call — this never happens here.
